A1.justification: Both readable, complete 22-page PDFs describe the same ACAVP study and include Appendices A–F. Pages 2–22 have identical extracted text and rendered appearance; the differences are confined to page 1.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification experiments, corruption robustness tests, ablations, and runtime measurements in Section 4, plus additional experiments in Appendix E.

after.justification: v2 retains the original empirical results in Section 4 and Appendix E, including classification, transferability, detection, and segmentation experiments.

M1.justification: The affine, color, and additive transformations, their constraints, and TrivialAugment training remain identical in Section 3 and Appendix C.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same twelve classification datasets, CIFAR corruption benchmarks, ImageNet, generative-model transfer scenarios, and PASCAL VOC detection and segmentation tasks.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged throughout: the main VP comparisons, Coordinator runtime comparisons, TVP generative-model comparison, and VPT comparison all retain their corresponding baseline sets.

E3.justification: Data splits, preprocessing, metrics, checkpoint selection, model configurations, and training budgets are identical in Section 4 and Appendices D–E.

E4.justification: Both versions retain the same transformation ablations, regularization comparisons, corruption robustness tests, Grad-CAM analysis, and hyperparameter sensitivity experiments, including Figures 2–3.

E5.justification: Section 4 retains three repetitions with average accuracy and standard error. Appendix E.4 retains its single-run specification; uncertainty reporting elsewhere is also unchanged.

E6.justification: All reported numerical and qualitative results are identical, including Tables 1–16 and Figures 2–3. For example, Table 2 retains ACAVP's 83.18% average accuracy, and Table 13 retains its 67.64% ImageNet accuracy.

T1.justification: Appendix B retains identical hypothesis-space definitions, Theorem B.1, Propositions B.2–B.3, and supporting mathematical reasoning. The method equations are also unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about transformation expressivity, overfitting mitigation, accuracy, robustness, and computational overhead. The added code-access sentence does not alter the scientific contributions.

C2.justification: Interpretations of component effects, generalization, and transferability are unchanged. Appendix F retains the same limitations concerning computational overhead and the restricted transformation family.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-availability statement and a link to the s-enmt/ACAVP GitHub repository at the end of the abstract; v1 supplies no code-access link. Implementation and experimental details remain unchanged. The PDFs establish the new access pointer, not the repository's contents or usability.

R1.justification: Section 2, Appendix A, and the reference list are identical. No cited works or substantive positioning relative to prior research are added or removed.

P1.justification: The abstract gains one code-availability sentence, and the arXiv version/date stamp changes. The remaining prose, terminology, section order, and appendix structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: The added abstract sentence produces slight first-page text reflow. All figures, tables, captions, and page layouts from page 2 onward remain visually identical.

improvement.justification: The new repository pointer makes the implementation easier to locate and modestly improves reproducibility guidance absent from v1. Scientific content, evidence, and limitations remain unchanged. This benefit concerns documentation; the supplied PDFs do not establish whether the linked code is complete or executable.
